brief: Blitz argues current market weakness is a correction, not a crisis, though a real one is coming later. AI makes transactions cheaper without showing up in GDP, and labor disruption is real but, in his view, nothing like the Depression. Against crisis: sector correlations to the S&P 500 are narrow now (tech near 1, but staples and financials falling since April), unlike 2008-09 or the dot-com crash when correlations converged toward 1. High-yield tech spreads have widened but remain below prior wides, and HY-versus-investment-grade spreads show no debt-quality alarm. The real threat is later: a rolling 12-month deficit at 6.4% of GDP, with a primary deficit of 3.2% and interest expense at 3.2% of GDP (highest since 1992), collides with Fed tightening and AI-driven reshoring, while AI-driven deflation will not reach rent-driven core inflation. The Fed under Warsh will not cut until equities fall about 10%. Blitz puts December 50bp-hike odds near 50/50 versus roughly 10% priced, hinging on November payrolls, and expects the 10-year yield to reach 6% next year and eventually 8%. A major bear market is coming, just not yet.
